newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea seeks to relax overseas fund-raising.
newsitem.headline: South Korea seeks to relax overseas fund-raising.

text.p: South Korea's trade ministry said on Wednesday it would propose doubling foreign exchange borrowings for the purchase of locally-produced capital goods to $4 billion.
The ministry also said large business groups would be allowed to finance their overseas investment projects entirely by overseas borrowings.
The current limit for large companies' overseas financing was 70 percent of the value of their overseas projects.
The ministry said these were among measures it was preparing to improve the nation's industrial competitiveness and the worsening trade balance.
But ministry officials said the measures should be discussed with related ministries and government organisations before implementation.
To promote bond issuances abroad, the ministry said it was considering easing or totally abolishing minimum requirements such as credit ratings, profit levels and paid-in capital.
The ministry said small businesses in technology-intensive industries would be provided with tax incentives. Research and development activities would be exempted from taxes, the ministry said.
